ON THE 15 th OF JULY, 2024  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 29380 of 2024  DILIP SISODIA @ DEEPAK JAIN  Versus  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH  Appearance:

 ORDER Heard on IA No. 11090/2024 which is an application for ignoring the defect pointed by registry.
2 Counsel for applicant submits that he has filed copy of the orders dated 18.6.2024 and 27.2.2024 as such material defects have been cured.
3 In view of the above, IA is allowed and defect is hereby ignored.
4 This court has decided application under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. hence being tide up matter, this M.Cr.C. is listed before this Court.

5 This is Second application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant o f bail to the applicant/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.17/2023 dated - 03.04.2023 registered at Police Station - Crime Branch, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 409, 420 and 34 of IPC.

sentences.text: 6 Prosecution story, in brief is that Kalptaru Grih Nirman, Sarkari Sanstha Maryadit (hereinafter referred as society) is a registered Housing Development Cooperation.
Last election of Board of Directors was conducted on 2 MCRC-29380-2024 16.08.2017.
Sub-auditor Suresh Bhandari was appointed as Administrator of the society.
Thereafter, when Suresh Bhandari checked the accounts of society, he found major financial irregularities and embezzlement of big amount.
It was also found that a sum of Rs.4,89,27,472/- was embezzled in favor of Board of Director and present applicant.

On the basis of written complaint filed by Suresh Bhandari, on 03.04.2023, the FIR was Dilip Sisodia @ Deepak Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168099826/

sentences.text:
1 lodged against present applicant Dilip Sisodiya and members of Board of Directors i.e., co-accused persons/then chairman Kamlesh Jain, Deputy Chairman Sunny Jaiswal, Jeetendra Narayan Patel,
Shubhas Kanhaiyalal Patidar, Milan Giri, Darshan Pratap Singh Mehta, Shri Chanda, Jeetendra Patil and Smt. Madhu Khanta.
7 Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 3.4.2023.

Although his earlier bail application has been dismissed on merit on the basis that other co-accused persons are still absconding, but thereafter co-accused Prakash Giri (President of the society) has been arrested, not a single member of the society has made any complaint against the applicant, regarding the aforesaid transaction civil suit No. 175/2022 is pending before the 24th ADJ Indore.
The dispute between the parties is of civil nature but malafidely it has been given criminal colour.
The incident had taken place in the year 2019 but it has been reported after a delay of four years.

Investigation is over and charge sheet has been filed, applicant has preferred SLP before the Hon'ble Supreme court but the same has been dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to avail other remedies as may be available under the law.

The applicant is suffering from serious medical ailments since last two months, three times he has been hospitalized as proper treatment is not possible in the custody, the case is completely based upon documentary evidence, therefore, there is no 3 MCRC-29380-2024 apprehension of tempering with the evidence.
In view of the aforesaid change circumstances, it is prayed that applicant be enlarged on bail.

8 Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that applicant is a habitual offender, eight criminal cases of similar nature have been found against him, after rejecting his earlier bail application, there is no material change in the circumstances, no plausible reason has been given by applicant against which transaction he has received huge amount from the society in his bank account, therefore applicant does not deserve for bail.

9 In rebuttal, counsel for applicant submits that although six criminal cases have been found against the applicant but in one offence, FIR has been quashed and in all other criminal matters, the applicant has been enlarged on bail.
10 Both the parties heard and perused the case diary with due care.
11 So far as the medical ground of applicant is concerned, from perusal of the documents Annexure P-5, P-6 and P-7 it appears that applicant is suffering from severe cardiac issues.
He was admitted in MGM Hospital Indore on 8.6.2024 whereupon his MRI L/s spine was done and multilevel degenjerative disc was found on MRL.
Earlier on 3.8.2023 he was admitted in hospital, thereafter he was again hospitalized from 9.8.2023 to 25.8.2023.
Therefore, it appears that applicant is suffering from serious medical ailments which are life threatening problem.

At the time of deciding his first application for grant of bail, the main accused Prakash Giri who is President of said society was absconded, therefore, now arrest of main accused is material change in the circumstances, civil suit is still pending between both the parties, 4 MCRC-29380-2024 therefore, it appears that matter pertains to civil dispute also, case of Dilip Sisodia @ Deepak Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168099826/

sentences.text: 2 prosecution is based upon documentary evidence, therefore, possibility of tempering with the evidence is not easy, investigation is over and charge sheet has been filed, applicant has been enlarged on bail in other matters and he did not misuse the liberty granted to him, he has already suffered jail incarceration of more than one year.
In these changed circumstances, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

12 It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.
1,00,000/- (Rupees One lakh Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C. Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Dilip Sisodia @ Deepak Jain vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/168099826/
